title: Long Mott (Dow / X-energy): U.S. Nuclear Regulatory Commission Establishing Fixed Fee Cap for Ongoing Long Mott Generating Station Construction Permit Application Review (EPIDs: L-2025-CPS-0000, L-2025-CPE-0000, and L-2026-HRG-0002) [['Letter']]

documents.text:
September 28, 2026


Mark Feltner
Technology Principal, Nuclear Power
Long Mott Energy, LLC
530 Gaither Road, Suite 700
Rockville, MD 20850

SUBJECT:       U.S. NUCLEAR REGULATORY COMMISSION ESTABLISHING FIXED FEE
               CAP FOR ONGOING LONG MOTT GENERATING STATION CONSTRUCTION
               PERMIT APPLICATION REVIEW (EPIDS: L-2025-CPS-0000,
               L-2025-CPE-0000, AND L-2026-HRG-0002)

Dear Mr. Feltner:

In preparation for the Executive Order 14300 fixed fee caps to take effect on October 1, 2026, a
fixed fee cap must be established by September 30, 2026, for each requested activity for which
a complete application has been accepted for review by the U.S. Nuclear Regulatory
Commission (NRC) before October 1, 2026, if the review will continue past October 1, 2026.

In accordance with Title 10 of the Code of Federal Regulations (10 CFR) 170.33, this
communication establishes the fixed cap on service fees (fixed fee cap) for the NRC’s review of
the Long Mott Generating Station (LMGS) construction permit (CP) application. The fixed fee
cap for the NRC’s review of this requested activity is $6,806,000. The NRC considered various
factors when establishing this fixed fee cap, such as the quality and complexity of the
application, technology type, and any pre-application engagement. The Reduced Hourly Rate
as established in 10 CFR 170.20(b) applies to this requested activity as of the statutory effective
date for the Reduced Hourly Rate (October 1, 2025).

The fixed fee cap represents the maximum amount that the NRC may charge for service fees
for this requested activity following acceptance of the complete application. The fixed fee cap
will not be increased except in instances of applicant failure, as defined in 10 CFR 170.3. If
applicant failure occurs, the NRC will notify Long Mott Energy, LLC., in writing of the new fixed
fee cap, which will be set at the lowest practicable amount determined by the NRC to account
for the applicant failure and complete the review.

The NRC will track service fees against the fixed fee cap beginning on May 12, 2025, which is
the date a complete application was accepted for review by the NRC for this requested activity.
 M, Feltner                                   2


Disputes associated with a fixed fee cap must be submitted in accordance with 10 CFR 15.31
and 170.33(f) and NRC Form 529 procedures.

                                          Sincerely,


                                                         Signed by Alissa Neuhausen on 09/28/26



                                          Alissa Neuhausen, Chief
                                          Advanced Reactor Engineering Branch 1
                                          Division of Advanced Reactor Engineering
                                          Office of Advanced Reactors
